_what: Per-task and per-certification writer instructions for ISMS-IA, printed into the writer prompt. A ruling about CONTENT does not belong in a code edit, and a note nobody can see in the artifact is a note nobody can check: the notes used are listed at the top of every run.
_cert_notes_what: `cert_notes` reaches THIS certification only. The mechanism exists because two ISMS-F rulings were sitting in the shared system prompt and were printed into an ISMS-IA prompt (found PROMPT-125 s5, moved PROMPT-126 s2). The tier's anchoring rule is NOT here -- it is computed from the certification code in lib/tier-anchoring.mjs, so it cannot drift from the gate.
cert_notes:
EVERY DISTRACTOR MUST BE A MISTAKE SOMEONE COULD ACTUALLY MAKE (ruled PROMPT-127 s4):

- Every distractor must be a mistake a working auditor or ISMS manager could plausibly make. No
  option may be rejectable on common sense alone. Prefer a short scenario that requires applying
  the clause over asking for the definition.
- This is why three of thirteen items were rejected on the first ISMS-IA round: a "visit calendar
  the certification body sets", "headcount", "the cheapest controls available", and a strawman
  naming a certification body's major nonconformities. Each was answerable by elimination without
  knowing the clause, which makes the item measure nothing.

3.5.instruction: This task is about INTERVIEW PRACTICE: which question form elicits evidence rather than confirmation. Key on ISO 19011 A.17 (Conducting interviews). ISO 19011 3.10 is a DEFINITION of audit evidence and a key resting on 3.10 alone is not interview practice -- use it for context or distractor support, not as the key's anchor.
